C_NAME: Air Quality Indicator - Ozone (O3) - CES, census tracts [ppm]
C_TOOLTIP: Air Quality Indicator - Ozone (O3) - CES, census tracts [ppm]. Ozone pollution causes numerous adverse health effects, including acute upper and lower respiratory symptoms, reduced lung function, and exacerbation of lung disease. CalEnviroScreen values modeled from 2011–2013 summer month maximum-value means. Values range from 0.03–0.07 ppm. EPA standard: "High" is > 0.07 ppm.

C_NAME: Air Quality Indicator - PM2.5 - CES, census tracts [mcg/cubic meter]
C_TOOLTIP: Air Quality Indicator - Fine Particulate Matter ≤ 2.5 microns - CES, census tracts [micrograms / cubic meter]. PM2.5 includes extremely small particles and liquid droplets that when inhaled can penetrate deep into the lungs causing serious health problems. CalEnviroScreen values modeled from 2012–2014 averages of quarterly means. Values range from 1.65–19.6 micrograms / cubic meter. EPA standard: "High" is > 12 micrograms / cubic meter.

C_NAME: Drinking Water Quality Indicator
C_TOOLTIP: The drinking water contaminant indicator considers measured chemical and bacterial contaminant levels; presence of multiple contaminants; and any past water system water-quality violations. CalEnviroScreen data (2005–2013) were aggregated from census blocks to tracts, weighted by population, and the state percentile value for each contaminant and violation type was summed for the overall score. The index ranges from 0 upwards, with higher values indicating greater concentrations of multiple contaminants.

C_NAME: Population Density [persons/square km]
C_TOOLTIP: Population density measures the number of persons per geographical area by dividing the total population by the total land area. It varies considerably across urban and rural areas and also across neighborhoods within cities. Values from ACS.

C_NAME: Unemployment Rate - Age 16 or Over
C_TOOLTIP: Estimated unemployment rate for persons age 16 and older. Values from ACS.

C_NAME: Burden - Child Dependency Ratio
C_TOOLTIP: The Child Dependency Ratio compares the size of the child population (age 17 and under) to the size of the working-age population (18–64) to measure the social and economic impact of age structures. The ratio ranges from zero upwards; the higher the number, the greater the burden of supporting children on working people. Values from ACS.

C_NAME: Burden - Old Age Dependency Ratio
C_TOOLTIP: The Old Age Dependency Ratio compares the size of the senior population (age 65 and over) to the size of the working-age population (18–64) to measure the social and economic impact of age structures. The ratio ranges from zero upwards; the higher the number, the greater the burden of supporting seniors on working people. Values from ACS.

C_METADATAXML: <?xml version="1.0"?><ValueMetadata><Version>3.02</Version><CreationDateTime>06/06/2021 18:00:00</CreationDateTime><TestID>SEDoH:SB535DisadvCmnty</TestID><TestName>Index - SB535 Disadvantaged Community?</TestName><DataType>Enum</DataType><Loinc>99999-9</Loinc><Flagstouse></Flagstouse><Oktousevalues>Y</Oktousevalues><MaxStringLength>255</MaxStringLength><EnumValues><Val description="Disadvantaged Commnity">Y</Val><Val description="Not a Disadvantaged Community">N</Val></EnumValues><UnitValues><NormalUnits></NormalUnits></UnitValues></ValueMetadata>
C_TOOLTIP: Census tract designated a SB 535 Disadvantaged Community. These communities represent the highest-scoring 25% most-pollution-burdened census tracts in California based on a suite of CalEnviroScreen indicators. SB 535 communities are specifically targeted for investment aimed at improving public health, quality of life, and economic opportunities, funded by proceeds from the Stateâ€™s cap-and-trade program, one of several strategies used to reduce greenhouse gases that cause climate change.

C_NAME: Index - Social Vulnerability Index
C_TOOLTIP: Social vulnerability measures community resilience to respond to or recover from threats to public health. The CDC SVI uses Census data for 15 social factors, including poverty, lack of access to transportation, and crowded housing, grouped into four themes. The index ranges from 0 to 1, with higher values indicating more-vulnerable populations.

  • Hover over a concept for more info (tooltips).

  • Note: Exposures to SEDoH measures should not be filtered with a date constraint.  A "temporal query" can be used to define a sequence of events, and this can establish a temporal constraint.  For details on temporal queries, click on "Help" on the upper right, and navigate to topic 3.2.3.

C_NAME:
About Air Quality Indicators
  • For "CES" measures, these are average measures for California census tracts, prepared by CalEnviroScreen/Cal EPA.  Data were released in 2018.
  • For "SCEHSC" measures, these are estimated ambient air pollution, interpolated to a 1-sq.km. grid from the 4 closest measurement stations.  This mapping was provided by SCEHSC/KSOM Preventive Medicine.  Data were collected in 1998–2009.
